text: Part 1. First, review questions 1-5. Good morning, Citywide Recruitment. How can I help? Hi, I'd like to register with your agency to look for work. Certainly, I can take your details now. Can I start with your name? Yes, my first name is Daniel and my surname is Farrelly. Could you spell the surname? Of course. F-A-R-R-E-L-L-Y. Thanks. I ask because we sometimes receive applications with a single letter missing and then an employer cannot match the paperwork to the person. Have you registered with Citywide before? No, this is my first time. I moved here at the beginning of the month so I am still finding out which firms recruit locally. In that case I should explain the process. Today I will create your profile and discuss the roles that might suit you. If you decide to apply for one, we send your details to the employer only after you have approved the job description. There is no charge to you at any stage. That sounds straightforward. Thank you. And the best number to reach you on? It's my mobile, 07816 445 230. Let me just check. 07816 445 230. Great. Now, what kind of work are you looking for? I was thinking warehouse work. Actually, no, I'd really prefer office administration. That's where my strengths are. Administration, good. And when would you be available to start? I'm free immediately. I finished my last contract a fortnight ago. That gives us some flexibility. Are you hoping for a permanent post? Or would you consider another temporary contract while you look? My preference is permanent work. but I would accept a contract lasting at least six months. I would rather avoid a very short placement because I want time to learn the organization properly. And would a journey across town be manageable? Yes, provided the office is near a bus route. I do not drive, but the buses from my neighborhood are reliable until quite late. Excellent, employers love that. Do you have relevant experience? Now review. You. Questions 6-10 before the recording continues. Most of my background is in retail. I managed a small shop for three years, so I'm used to dealing with customers and paperwork. That's useful. And your highest qualification? I have a diploma in business studies. Noted. One more thing. Do you speak any other languages? Some of our clients value that. Yes, I speak French fairly fluently. Excellent. What computer skills should I put down? Employers often ask specifically about spreadsheets and diary systems. I use word processing and spreadsheet software every day, and in my last job I organized the manager's electronic diary. I also dealt with invoices. I have not used specialist accounting software, though. That's fine. We can offer a short online course if a vacancy requires it. I should also ask about working hours. You mentioned public transport, so would early mornings be difficult? A start before seven would be awkward. Normal office hours are ideal, and I could occasionally stay late. I am also available on Saturdays, although I would prefer not to work every weekend. Good. I'll note all of that. References can wait until an employer requests them, but it helps to warn two former supervisors now. I can contact my previous manager and the owner of the shop today. Wonderful. Now, let me tell you about a few vacancies we have. First, there's a receptionist role in the city center, full-time, paying 11 pounds and 50 pence an hour. Then we have an office assistant position. That one's out at Riverside, it's part-time, and it pays 12 pounds an hour. and finally a data clerk job, also in the city center, but the hours are evenings only at 13 pounds an hour. The office assistant one sounds ideal actually. It does seem the closest match. The receptionist post involves a lot of face-to-face work and starts at half past seven while the data clerk role is quieter but finishes after the last bus to your area. At Riverside, the office may extend the hours after the first three months. That timetable would be perfect. What would I actually be doing? Mostly arranging appointments, preparing simple reports, and answering email inquiries. There is some telephone work, but another colleague covers the reception desk. They want someone accurate and calm rather than someone with a particular degree. That sounds close to what I did in the shop office. Exactly. Your customer experience is relevant and your business qualification supports the administrative side. Before I submit the application, send me your latest employment dates. You can attach them to the reply when my message arrives. Great. I'll put you forward for it. I'll email you the full description this afternoon and we'll arrange an interview. Thank you so much for your help.
